correctness.rationale: The span of mutually annihilating pure tensors contains arrow-arrow tensors, unequal vertex pairs and mixed pairs at nonincident vertices. For each nonloop i→j, the mutually annihilating pairs (e_i+a,e_j−a) and (e_j+a,e_i−a) identify the two pairs of mixed cosets, leaving at most two generators per arrow, including loops. For a loop, the e_i coefficient of xy is the product of the two vertex coefficients, and if the first is nonzero the loop coefficient of xy then forces the second argument's loop coefficient to vanish. Hence each stated loop form vanishes on zero products. Testing on e_i⊗a−a⊗e_i pairs these forms with the identity matrix and kills all product forms. The product-pair map has independent generators (e_i,e_i), the two single-coordinate generators per nonloop, and the diagonal generator per loop. This yields the asserted dimensions, basis, decomposition and counts over any field, including characteristic two; no restriction on cycles or multiplicities is needed. The frozen finite-field checker was inspected, not run; it is illustrative and not required by the algebraic proof.
